Peru.name: Lake Titicaca
Peru.note: Highest navigable lake in the world (~3,812 m); shared with Bolivia, sacred in Inca cosmology.

Bolivia.name: Lake Titicaca
Bolivia.note: Highest navigable lake in the world (~3,812 m); shared with Peru, sacred in Inca cosmology.

Venezuela.name: Lake Maracaibo
Venezuela.note: Largest lake in South America; a brackish tidal bay at its mouth — centre of Venezuela's oil industry.

Venezuela.name: Angel Falls
Venezuela.note: World's highest uninterrupted waterfall (979 m), on a tributary of the Caroní in Canaima National Park.

Canada.name: Great Bear Lake
Canada.note: Largest lake entirely within Canada; deep in the Northwest Territories.

United States.name: Lake Superior
United States.note: Largest of the Great Lakes by area — shared with Canada, on the US–Canada border.

Kenya.name: Lake Victoria
Kenya.note: Africa's largest lake by area; source of the White Nile, shared with Uganda and Tanzania.

Chad.name: Lake Chad
Chad.note: Shrunk by over 90% since the 1960s — a textbook case of desertification, shared by four countries.

Russia (European).name: Lake Ladoga
Russia (European).note: Largest lake in Europe; supplied the 'Road of Life' into besieged Leningrad in WWII.

Switzerland.name: Lake Geneva
Switzerland.note: Crescent-shaped Alpine lake shared with France; Geneva sits at its southwestern tip.

Kazakhstan.name: Caspian Sea
Kazakhstan.note: World's largest inland body of water — technically a sea, bordered by five countries.

Kazakhstan.name: Aral Sea (remnant)
Kazakhstan.note: Shrunk drastically since the 1960s after Soviet-era irrigation diverted its feeder rivers.

Nepal.name: Rara Lake
Nepal.note: Nepal's largest lake, in a remote Himalayan national park.

Australia.name: Lake Eyre
Australia.note: Australia's lowest point and largest lake — usually a dry salt pan, filling only in rare floods.
